_readme: Hand-authored social posts. This is the only file in social/ that is committed.
Captions are English only; the blog carries Spanish.
Posts go out 5:00 PM America/Chicago — DST-aware, see scripts/lib/ghl.mjs.
Validate with: npm run social:validate   Dry run: npm run social:schedule

posts.caption:
Meet-the-teacher night is this week for most of Kaufman County.

The honest read from teachers: they get a lot of mugs, and a lot of apple-themed things. What they're short on is something that makes the first week easier.

Greenleaf scented sachet — $1.50, goes in a desk drawer
"Great Teacher Change Lives" mug — $20
Teacher notebook — $12
Teacher keychain — $16
Kaweco Sport pen — $28, for the one who writes constantly

Handle it the week before, not the night of. The night-of crowd is real.

Lunchbox season. Swig is the wall that solves it.

BOXXI lunch boxes — $27.20
Oh Happy Day lunch bag — $34
Iced cup coolie — $13
Mega mug pouch — $15.95
22oz travel mugs — $33.60 to $42

The insulated bottles hold ice through a Texas school day, which in August is the entire point. And yes, a good share of these go to the adult in the car line. No judgment.

Week one is when the high schooler discovers they have five teachers and no system.

Notebooks $12 to $18 — "You Got This," "Do Your Best," butterflies, colorful bows.

Paper planners are back with students, and the reason is simple: a phone calendar competes with every notification on the device. A notebook doesn't.

The under-$3 shelf, for when a kid has earned something small.

Charm pens — $1.70 to $2.15. Capybara, sea animals, safari animals, lollipop.

This is the aisle that buys you fifteen more minutes of shopping. We're not going to pretend otherwise.

Thirty-one keychains in stock, $9 to $16.

"be kind." "GOD is with me." Smiley stars. Seed bead apple for a teacher.

A backpack zipper is the most-seen surface a middle schooler owns. Worth letting them pick.

The birthday you forgot about until this morning.

Rain earrings from $13. Splendid Iris from $18. Voluspa mini tins at $16. Pampa Bay mini dishes from $8.

Fifteen minutes, wrapped at the counter, and you walk out with something that doesn't look like you bought it at a gas station on the way.

Suite 112, I-20 Exit 501. Tue-Sat 10-7, Sun 11-6.

Labor Day cookout this weekend? Don't bring more food.

The host has food. The host has drinks. What they don't have is something small and good that outlasts the weekend.

Greenleaf Citron Sol candle — $12
Crow Canyon enamelware plate — $14
Govino 2-pack — $15, unbreakable, correct Texas patio glassware
Voluspa 5.5 oz — $22
Crow Canyon oval platter — $36 to $40

Two or three gatherings? Buy them together, we'll wrap and tag each one.

Labor Day weekend hours, so nobody drives out on a guess:

Saturday Sep 5 — 10 AM to 7 PM
Sunday Sep 6 — 11 AM to 6 PM
Monday Sep 7 — CLOSED

We're closed Mondays, holiday included. If you need a host gift for a Monday cookout, Saturday or Sunday is your window. The outlet anchors keep their own holiday hours, so The Shops at Terrell is still a Monday option — just not us.

The scent shift has started.

Summer citrus is on its way out, the warm fall Voluspa is coming in. Mini tins at $16, the 9 oz classics and 18 oz jars at $34.

Come smell them. That part genuinely doesn't work through a screen, which is the one advantage a physical shop still has.

If you're hosting Thanksgiving, September is when to look. Not November.

Pampa Bay is in — mini square bowls from $8, heart dishes at $10, snack bowls at $14, up to a $54 footed bowl.

Here's the thing people learn the hard way: serving pieces don't get restocked in late November. What's on the shelf now is largely what there is.

The Julie Vos case just got restocked for fall.

Crescent Hoops start at $65. The Milano Luxe bangles are $125. The Honeybee statement necklace is $395 and it is exactly as good in person as it looks.

These come in small quantities and when a piece sells it usually doesn't come back that season. If there's someone specific in mind for December, October is when the piece still exists.

Gugu Gifts · Suite 112 · The Shops at Terrell

Probably not what you expect to find in Terrell: 143 pieces of Japanese stationery.

OSCOLABO carved rubber stamps from $7. Shachihata Iromoyo pigment ink at $12. Kaweco Lunar Sport pens at $28. Luddite canvas pen cases woven in Kurashiki, $18.

People come in for a candle and leave forty minutes later holding a stamp of a swallow in flight. Full guide on the blog.

Sixty-four pairs of Rain earrings in the case right now, starting at $13.

Silver, oxidized finishes, Southwestern and nature motifs — the kind of thing that reads as Texas without being a longhorn.

The blue butterfly pair at $13 is the cheapest thing in the store that still reads as real jewelry. Under $20 means you can buy it without a reason.

image.itemName: Gold Red Flowers & Bees Seven Post Earring Set

posts.caption:
The scent shift is done. Summer citrus is out, the warm fall Voluspa is in.

Mini tins at $16. The 9 oz classics at $34. Full 18 oz jars in Panjore Lychee and Baltic Amber, also $34.

If you've only ever bought the bright summer scents, the fall range is a genuinely different experience. Come smell them — that part doesn't work through a screen.

Seventy-eight pairs of Splendid Iris earrings, from $18.

Gold, clean, classic. Huggies, thin hoops, studs, alphabet initials. Less pattern, more shape.

If you genuinely don't know someone's taste, the 4mm gold huggies at $18 are the least wrong thing in the case. That's not a small compliment.

Close to 60 Ty in stock, from $6.99.

It is reliably the busiest three feet of the store between Thanksgiving and Christmas, and it solves four problems: stockings, party favors for a kid you barely know, the "one more small thing" gift, and keeping a child occupied while you shop.

LARA the capybara is the one that stops people mid-aisle.

The Kaweco wall: 22 Lunar Sport pens, ballpoint and rollerball, $28 each.

Octagonal barrel, pocket length, threads closed so it won't leak in a bag. German-made, adopted by Japanese stationery shops and never let go of.

This is our standard answer to "I need a gift for someone who writes constantly and has never owned a good pen."

Rain necklaces, $20 to $33.

Silver and turquoise, crystal sets, oxidized detail. The price band where jewelry stops being an occasion and starts being something you wear on a Tuesday.

Free wrapping at the counter, so you can walk in without a gift bag in the car.

image.itemName: Silver Big Blue Crystal Necklace Set

posts.caption:
Real gold under $85.

Brenda Grands: 18K Zenith hoops at $38, triple mini hoops at $48, a dainty diamond cross pendant at $53, 24K hammered hoops at $60.

This is the line for someone building a set they'll wear daily, rather than making a statement. It stacks with whatever they already own — which is why it's hard to get wrong.

Splendid Iris rings, $17 to $25.

Pave leaf adjustable, stacking bands, simple gold. Adjustable means you don't need to know a ring size, which removes the single most common reason a jewelry gift fails.

image.itemName: Ring - Pave leaf adjustable ring, Gold

posts.caption:
If you're buying one serious gift this season, start looking now.

Julie Vos runs $65 to $395 here. By mid-December the case is picked over — the popular bangles and the initial pieces go first, and initials go in an unpredictable order depending on which letters people need.

We'll hold a piece with a note. Costs you nothing and removes the December problem entirely.

We've been building gift boxes out of what's on our shelves.

A Mary Square notepad, a pen and a Gingerbread sachet — about $20.
Gorky González turtle shakers, a bird plate and a Voluspa tin — about $65.
A Western one with our Howdy and cowboy boot dishes.

Bring a budget and a name. We'll help you put one together and wrap it free. The pieces that make these work come in small numbers, so earlier is better.

The Shops at Terrell, I-20 Exit 501.

New in: interchangeable enamel pin sets.

The dim sum basket is the one everyone picks up first. Small, odd, specific — the kind of gift that gets remembered because nobody else thought of it.

image.itemName: Dim Sum Basket Interchangeable Enamel Pin Set

posts.caption:
Voluspa's ornament candles are in. Noble Fir Garland, Crushed Candy Cane and Gingerbread Chalet, $18 each.

They come boxed, with a ribbon loop so they hang on the tree. The coworker gift, sorted.

Forty-four Cardthartic cards in stock, from $2.

Illustrated, and they don't do the sentimental thing — the art carries it. Mini cards at $2, standard at $4.25, a boxed Flowery Hello collection at $14.

A $2 mini card attached to a $6 item turns two cheap things into one considered thing. That's most of gift-giving, honestly.

The Christmas earrings are out.

Rain Jewelry Santas, snowflakes, candy canes and ugly sweaters, $15 to $20. Most designs are one or two deep, so if you see the pair, that may be the pair.

About 25 minutes from Rockwall.

Last day for the Halloween earrings. Pumpkins, skeletons and Boo, $15 to $23.

Tomorrow the case turns over to Christmas. Open today until 7.

Splendid Iris necklaces, $14 to $43.

Quatrefoil shell pendants, delicate chains, layering pieces. Some of the studs come mounted on a velvet gift tag — including a red velvet Christmas tag that's already in.

That's a wrapped gift with no wrapping required, which is exactly what you want in December.

image.itemName: Necklace - Quatrefoil shell pendant with dotted border, Gold

posts.caption:
Gift boxes for anyone who needs a long bath.

Beekman 1802's White Chocolate Strawberry set ($36), a Pacha bath bomb ($9), a Greenleaf candle, and a Ty plush sitting on top. Most of these land between $50 and $80.

We'll build one with you and wrap it free.

Rain stretch bracelets — including 6-packs you can split up.

$19 and up. One pack covers several people, which is the actual problem most of you are solving in November.

image.itemName: Silver Design 6 Pack Metal Stretch Bracelets

posts.caption:
Twelve rollerball perfumes from Mixologie, $20 each, no alcohol. Glow, Tempted, Tenacious, Sensual, Adrift and the rest.

Can't pick one for her? The Tiny Try Me Kit is also $20, and she can find her own.

The Ty wall is at its fullest right now and at its thinnest the week before Christmas.

That's not a sales pitch, it's just how a small shop's reorder cycle works against the national supply of plush animals in December.

From $6.99. Buy stocking stuffers in November and you get selection. Buy them December 20th and you get what's left — same as everyone else in Kaufman County.

Kid-size gift boxes, about $25 to $40.

Pusheen gel pens, lip balm and nail stickers. Rudy Red the reindeer bath bomb with a Splendid Iris reindeer necklace. Frothy the Snowman with a Christmas tree necklace.

Built from our shelves, wrapped free.

For the reader: Studio Oh!'s Cozy Reads cosmetics bag, $22. Jane Eyre, Pride and Prejudice, Heidi.

The keychain pouches are $9 and clip to a backpack. The whole teen wall is about 15 minutes from Forney.

Gift boxes for her.

A Swig hydrangea Mega Mug with a manicure set and a Voluspa tin, around $90, or about $60 without the manicure set.
A lavender wristlet with Beekman lavender soap and hand cream.
A Demdaco travel jewelry case with a necklace.
Cow print and Howdy, for the Western one.

These pieces are only a few deep. Come in and we'll build it with you.

Voluspa gift sets are in.

The 2.5 oz best-sellers set is the one to reach for when you need something that looks considered and costs less than people assume. Singles from $16.

The safe, always-correct gift for a coworker, a neighbor, or a teacher.

Gorky González, hand-painted in Guanajuato. The Longhorn platter is $132, and there's one.

The mini animal plates are $16, the salt and pepper sets $28 to $32. Thanksgiving is a week out.

Friendsgiving weekend. The hostess gift that gets used on the day: Mary Square quick-dry Christmas kitchen towels, $14, or the dish towel bundles at $11.

Add a $15 Greenleaf candle and you're done.

Two days to Thanksgiving. Hand-painted Gorky González salt and pepper sets: turtles, donkeys, sheep. $28 to $32, wrapped free.

Open today and tomorrow, 10 to 7.

Mary Square's prayer journal has daily pages for your worries, praises, prayers and God's promises. $19, in pink or blue.

Sermon Notes is $18. For the Sunday school teacher, the small group, and Grandma.

Small Business Saturday at The Shops at Terrell.

Gugu Gifts is in Suite 112: Gorky González pottery, Voluspa, Beekman 1802, Rain and Splendid Iris jewelry, Swig, and a lot of Ty. Everything is wrapped free.

Open today 10 to 7. I-20 Exit 501.

Twelve coworkers, $42, wrapped.

Twelve Cardthartic mini cards ($24) plus twelve Greenleaf sachets ($18). Three-fifty a person and not one of them reads as cheap.

People spend $150 on a dozen mediocre small gifts every December. Under $15 is where most gifting actually happens and where most of it goes wrong. Full guide on the blog.

Pacha's 12 Days of Bath Bombs, $33. An advent calendar for someone who'd rather have a bath than a chocolate.

Start it on the 25th and it runs into January.

Gingerbread Holly, Snowman Jake and Gouda Mouse. Ty, $6.99 each.

Our stocking stuffer guide is up: everything under $20, most of it under $10. 15 minutes east of Forney on I-20.

Christmas squishies, $10. Santa, a reindeer, a snowman and a tree.

Labeled 3+. Bought mostly by 12-year-olds and adults with stressful jobs.

Christmas tree studs on red velvet gift tags, $18. The tag is the packaging, so it's wrapped without wrapping.

The same tags come in snowflakes, red bows, green-and-red pear CZ, hearts and tiny crosses. A few of each left.

Christmas pins are back. The pearl tree is $23, the stocking $20, the cardinal birdhouse $25.

The gift for Grandma that she'll wear to church this Sunday.

Swig's 30 oz Mega Mug, $44. Tile, hydrangea, cherry.

The gift for anyone who already carries a tumbler everywhere, which is most of Kaufman County. Wrapped free.

Still time.

We wrap everything free, we're open Tuesday through Saturday 10–7 and Sunday 11–6, and there is a real person here who will help you pick something rather than pointing at a shelf.

301 Tanger Dr, Suite 112, Terrell. I-20 Exit 501. Closed Mondays.

Eight days. Everything we sell gets wrapped free at the counter. Walk in, pick, walk out with it done.

Open Tuesday to Saturday 10 to 7, Sunday 11 to 6. Closed Monday the 21st.

Last Saturday before Christmas.

Voluspa's Fruit & Floral Travel Trio, three eau de parfums in a holiday box, $42. Already boxed, and we'll wrap it anyway. Open until 7.

Open today and tomorrow, 10 to 7.

Well Kept screen wipes in Ho Ho Cocoa and plaid, $7. The stocking stuffer for everyone who owns a phone.

Everything wrapped free.
